title: Chaos
summary: A family of precise but non-equivalent dynamical notions rather than one universal predicate.

content.human: “Chaos” has several rigorous definitions. QEVA should name the definition being used instead of treating the word as self-explanatory.
content.exact: QEVA Protocol 0.1 assigns no universal predicate Chaos(T). A record claiming chaos must identify a contextual criterion (for example a named topological, measure-theoretic, symbolic, or metric definition) and state its hypotheses.
content.example: A map may satisfy sensitive dependence while failing some stronger named chaos criterion.
content.caveat: Popular descriptions such as “random-looking” or “small errors grow” are not by themselves mathematical definitions of chaos.

verification.method: Definition checked for internal consistency; not yet linked to an external formal proof artifact.

provenance.creator: QEVA seed archive
provenance.source_note: Seed record written to demonstrate QEVA Protocol 0.1; it is not claimed to be the unique foundational presentation of this concept.
